Allowed, subject to all just exceptions.
2. Application stands disposed of.

3. The instant petition under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Cr.P.C) has been filed by the petitioners praying for quashing of FIR bearing no. 375/2020, registered at Police Station Maurya Enclave, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom.
4. Issue notice.
Mr. Satish Kumar, learned APP accepts notice on behalf of the State.

5. All the petitioners are present before this Court and have been identified by their counsel Ms.
Priyanka Singh and Investigating Officer (IO) SI Radha Kanwar from Police Station Maurya Enclave.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner no. 1 and respondent no. 2 had been solemnized on 07.03.2019 according to Hindu rites, customs and ceremonies at Uttar Pradesh.
Due to some temperamental differences and misunderstanding between both of them, they have been residing separately since 04.06.2019.

It is stated that on the complaint of Uttam Singh & Ors vs State Of Nct Of Delhi & Anr on 21 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56736613/
1 complainant/respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing no.375/2020 was registered at Police Station Maurya Enclave, for the offences punishable under Section 498A/406/34 of IPC against petitioners.

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no. 2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.

It is also stated by respondent no. 2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement/Agreement dated 22.07.2022 before Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, Delhi.
8.

entities.text: Delhi Mediation Centre, Rohini District Courts, Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
It is submitted that respondent no. 2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner no. 1 and other family members.

9. The petitioner no. 1 had paid a sum of Rs. 15,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:
a. First installment of Rs. 5,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in first motion.
b. Second instalment of Rs. 5,00,000/- paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of recording of statement in second motion.
c.
Third/final instalment of Rs. 5,00,000/- to be paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of quashing of FIR before Honble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 5,00,000/- today, i.e., 21.03.2023 vide DD No. 178851 drawn on HDFC Bank,
Greater Kailash-II, New Delhi and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above facts that the parties have amicably resolved their differences out of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings, rather the same would create further acrimony between them.
It would thus be in interest of justice to quash the abovementioned FIR and the proceedings pursuant thereto.
There is no legal impediment in quashing the FIR in question.

12. Accordingly, FIR bearing no. 375/2020, registered at Police Station Maurya Enclave, Delhi, for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406/34 of the IPC and all consequential proceedings emanating therefrom are quashed.
13. The present petition stands disposed of.
